quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You should always travel at a speed that is:

options.text: The same as the vehicles around you.
Right for the road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right for the road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: How fast you drive depends on road conditions, weather, and the speed limit. Never drive faster than the speed limit. Slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: For a person 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent or higher.
questions.explanation: For drivers 21 and older, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is illegal. Driving under the influence of alcohol is dangerous and against the law.

questions.question: You drive defensively when you:

options.text: Keep one car length between you and the car ahead.
Look only at the car directly in front of you.
Keep your eyes moving to spot dangers ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your eyes moving to spot dangers ahead.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means scanning the road ahead for potential dangers. Do not stare only at the road right in front of you. Look ahead and be alert to traffic around you.

questions.question: Which statement is true about work zones on roads?

options.text: Traffic violations in work zones have the same fines as normal traffic violations.
You must slow down in work zones.
Only slow down if you see workers present.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must slow down in work zones.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop for road equipment in work zones. Careful driving in work zones keeps drivers, pedestrians, bicyclists, and road workers safe.

questions.question: Give the right-of-way to pedestrians who are:
questions.correctAnswerText: Crossing any street.
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing in marked or unmarked crosswalks. For safety, drivers should yield to anyone crossing a street.

questions.question: A red traffic light is showing, but a police officer tells you to go through the intersection. You should:

options.text: Stop until the light turns green.
Come to a complete stop first, then proceed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through the intersection.
questions.explanation: Always follow a police officer's directions. Police instructions override traffic signals and signs.

questions.question: When parallel parking, you should park within ____ inches of the curb.
questions.explanation: When parallel parking, stay no more than 18 inches from the curb. Park where other drivers can see your vehicle from both directions.

questions.question: When parallel parking downhill, you should:

options.text: Turn your wheels sharply toward the curb.
Turn your wheels away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels sharply toward the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your front wheels toward the curb. When parking uphill without a curb, turn wheels toward the edge. When parking uphill with a curb, turn wheels away from the curb.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are what color?
questions.correctAnswerText: White.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what laws they must follow. They control traffic direction, lane use, turning, speed, parking, and special situations. These signs are usually white rectangles with black, red, or green text or symbols.

questions.question: When turning left from a two-way street, you should drive:

options.text: Near the right side of the road.
On the left side of the center line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the center line.
questions.explanation: When turning left, start in the lane closest to the center line. Begin your turn just before reaching the intersection center. Do not cut the corner. Turn into the first legal lane.

questions.question: To turn quickly, your hands should be:

options.text: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
Next to each other on top of the steering wheel.
On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Place both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel. This position is comfortable and allows you to turn safely at high speeds.

questions.question: This sign warns of a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that your road ends at an intersection ahead. Slow down and prepare to yield or stop before turning left or right.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should always:

options.text: Look left and right to see what is coming.
Slowly pass vehicles that are stopped with no reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left and right to see what is coming.
questions.explanation: At any place where people may cross your path or where traffic streams meet, look left and right to ensure it is safe to proceed.

questions.question: How do you make room for cars entering the freeway?
questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane.
questions.explanation: Make room for cars entering the freeway. If you can, move to another lane to create space. If you cannot move lanes, adjust your speed so the entering cars can merge safely and smoothly.

questions.question: If dust or smoke blocks your view of other vehicles, you should drive slowly and turn on your:
questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights whenever you cannot see other vehicles clearly. Other drivers may also have trouble seeing you.

questions.question: This red and white sign means you should:

options.text: Stop and look for traffic from both directions before going.
Let traffic on the road you want to enter or cross go first.
Keep a steady speed and check for traffic from all directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let traffic on the road you want to enter or cross go first.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means you must slow down and be ready to stop if needed. Let any vehicle, bike rider, or pedestrian pass before you go. You do not have the right-of-way.

questions.question: At a "Yield" sign, you must:

options.text: Let cross traffic that is close enough to cause a crash go first.
Let only vehicles on your right go first.
Always slow down and go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let cross traffic that is close enough to cause a crash go first.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down or stop if needed. Let crossing or merging vehicles go first. Give the right-of-way to any traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.

questions.question: When should you give up your right-of-way?
questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever it helps prevent crashes.
questions.explanation: Do not assume other drivers will give you the right-of-way. Give up your right-of-way whenever it helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, drive at:

options.text: The same speed as freeway traffic.
5 to 10 mph slower than freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same speed as freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging onto a freeway, drive at or near the speed of traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: You park uphill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should your front wheels point?

options.text: Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking uphill or downhill with no curb, turn your wheels so your car rolls away from the road center if your brakes fail.

questions.question: When passing another car, return to your lane when:

options.text: You see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror.
You have cleared the front bumper of the other car.
You are 50 feet ahead of the other car.

questions.correctAnswerText: You see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When passing, return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the other car in your mirror. This ensures you have enough space to safely move back in front of them.

questions.question: A driver license is a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege, not a right.
questions.explanation: A driver license is not a right. It is a privilege you must earn and keep.

questions.question: A car suddenly cuts in front of you. What should you do first?
questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a car cuts in front of you too close, take your foot off the gas. This creates space without hard braking or swerving into another lane.

questions.question: Broken yellow lines separate:

options.text: Lanes of traffic going the same direction.
Lanes of traffic going opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lanes of traffic going opposite directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Broken lines mean passing is allowed when it is safe.

questions.question: If hit from the rear, you should consider all of the following except:

options.text: Letting go of the steering wheel.
Pressing your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Letting go of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If hit from the rear, your body will be thrown backward. Press yourself against the seat and put your head against the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Hold the steering wheel firmly and be ready to brake to avoid hitting the car in front of you.
